s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging mass on the wrist with median nerve compression
salient_findings: Mass on the anterior aspect of the right wrist
Biphasic contrast enhancement on MRI (target sign)
key_facts: 1-year history of a gradually enlarging mass
Mass located on the anterior aspect of the right wrist
Mass located along the radial edge
Phalen’s maneuver was positive
Durkan’s test was positive
Median nerve compression was indicated
MRI showed a well-defined, encapsulated mass
Mass exhibited biphasic contrast enhancement (target sign)
Mass located on the radial side of the wrist

shortlist: Giant Cell Tumor of Tendon Sheath

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Tumor of Tendon Sheath
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of a gradually enlarging mass on the wrist with median nerve compression

shortlist.label: Ganglion Cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Typical presentation of a well-defined, encapsulated mass on the wrist with biphasic contrast enhancement

shortlist.label: Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by a target sign on MRI, consistent with the patient's imaging findings

shortlist.label: Glomus Tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause median nerve compression and present as a well-defined mass on the wrist

shortlist.label: Nodular Tenosynovitis
shortlist.why_kept: May present with a gradually enlarging mass and median nerve compression, similar to the patient's symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a gradually enlarging mass on the wrist with positive Phalen's and Durkan's tests indicating median nerve compression, along with MRI findings of a well-defined, encapsulated mass with biphasic contrast enhancement (target sign), is most consistent with a ganglion cyst.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Tumor of Tendon Sheath
rejected.why: While possible, the biphasic contrast enhancement and specific location are more characteristic of a ganglion cyst.

rejected.label: Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma
rejected.why: This condition is less common and the clinical presentation does not specifically suggest this diagnosis over ganglion cyst.

rejected.label: Glomus Tumor
rejected.why: Glomus tumors are typically very painful and have a distinct blue color, which was not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Nodular Tenosynovitis
rejected.why: The clinical and imaging findings do not align closely with nodular tenosynovitis, which typically involves the tendon sheath and does not exhibit the target sign on MRI.
